applicability.scope: MLX-LM generation, batch-row and prefix-cache diagnosis; model/backend/runtime compatibility requires separate qualification.
applicability.prerequisites: Access to the independently pinned MLX-LM generation/cache contracts and the selected entry path; model, backend and runtime compatibility is separately established for any native claim.
applicability.input_contract: MLX-LM/MLX revisions and builds, backend/device, model/tokenizer/adapter/draft identities, entry point, tokenized prompts, cache classes, batching/prefill limits, per-request sampling/processors/stops, seed and KV quantization; failure traces include UIDs, stages, lengths, terminal reason and next-request result.
applicability.produced_artifact: An entry-path decision, UID/stage/cache-row table, prefix identity and cache-class assumptions, terminal/cleanup trace and actual evidence status with a targeted verification plan.
applicability.failure_modes: Ignoring server batching gates, filtering only some per-request row state, reusing a text-only prefix key or treating a stop flag as immediate MLX work cancellation can corrupt lifecycle reasoning.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop at the first unsupported contract or missing required fixture/backend; retain a targeted plan without inferring paged allocation, radix sharing or instantaneous prefill interruption.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local native-backend, model, service or efficacy validation.
Static content checks do not promote this candidate or establish installed API conformance.
recommendations: Resolve the library versus server entry and its batching gates before transferring BatchGenerator behavior.
Keep UID, caches, tokens, samplers, processors, lengths, stop matchers and pending outputs aligned under the same removal selection, including prompt-stage requests.
Check exact token/model/adapter/draft identity and cache-type copy/trim semantics, then trace cooperative removal through survivor and next-request behavior.
